normalization: The Archive's own OCR layer of this volume reads the Greek as Latin and is not used. The PDF named in origin.items was rasterized page by page at 300 dpi (pdftoppm -r 300 -gray) and each page OCR'd in session; the OCR is kept as made, line endings normalized, one '=== p<N> ===' line before each PDF page. No text was corrected by hand; the loci keep the OCR's readings and say where those differ from the printed page. The volume is divided into works at its running heads (rebuild/corpora/ea-corpora-33/split_bergk33.py), corrected by reading the boundary pages; a page carrying the end of one section and the start of the next goes with the later. Bergk's Greek is printed with his Latin apparatus beneath; the OCR keeps both.
scope: The volume entire in session OCR, 764 PDF pages, divided at its running heads into 35 sections: Eumelus, Terpander, Alcman, Arion, Sappho, Erinna, Alcaeus, the sages' songs, Stesichorus, Ibycus, Anacreon with the Anacreontea, Lasus, Telesilla, Simonides, Timocreon, Corinna, Lamprocles, Pratinas, Diagoras, Praxilla, the Bacchylides fragments, Melanippides, Licymnius, Philoxenus, Timotheus, Telestes, Castorio, Hermodotus, the scolia, the carmina popularia and the fragmenta adespota, with the index. Pindar is in Bergk's vol. I and seated from Perseus (33/02); the papyri published after 1882 are in Edmonds (33/05) and the papyri panel (01/11).
verified_loci: Sappho 1 (Bergk), the hymn to Aphrodite: its first word — 'Ποικιλόϑρον᾽, ἀϑάνατ᾽' (the page reads Ἀφρόδιτα after it; the OCR reads Aqpódua)
Sappho 2 (Bergk; 31 in later numbering), the opening line — 'Φαίνεταί μοι κῆνος ἴσος ϑέοισιν'
Alcman, the Louvre Partheneion: there is a vengeance of the gods — 'ἔστι τις σιῶν τίσις'
Corinna, the rebuke of Myrtis — 'Μέμφομη δὲ κὴ λιγουρὰν Μουρτίδ᾽ ἰώνγα'
Carmina popularia, the Rhodian swallow song — 'ἦλϑε χελιδών'
why_seated: The operator asked for all of Sappho and all the melic poets, seated with Tacitus: song and silence. Bergk's fourth edition is the last complete nineteenth-century collection of the melic fragments, public domain everywhere, in Greek with its Latin apparatus.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-11-04: "and I suppose we should seat tacitus" (11:28 EST); "we currently have only sappho 31 i believe. we need all sappho and all the melic poets. what an oversight. they can go together with tacitus, song and silence at one seat" (11:29 EST); "corinna definitely... im not familiar with telesilla or the carmina popularia but yet lets seat the" (11:46 EST); on Edmonds, "yes, lets seat it with the statement" (11:54 EST).
seating: EA-CORPORA-33, the thirty-third seating: song and silence — Tacitus, and Sappho whole with the melic poets, 2026-11-04
